title: The robust spectrum: multitaper PSD of occipital alpha, checked against scipy DPSS and MNE

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb)
dataset.record: subject S001, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed rest), occipital channel O1, first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples)
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: A single periodogram of a short EEG segment is noisy -- its variance does not shrink as you record longer. The multitaper method (Thomson 1982) fixes this: it passes the signal through a family of orthogonal DPSS (Slepian) tapers, takes a periodogram through each, and averages them -- trading a little frequency resolution for a large drop in variance and controlled spectral leakage. On real eyes-closed occipital EEG the ecosystem's eegMultitaper computes this robust spectrum and it is alpha-dominated (peak at 10.5 Hz, 46% of the 0-45 Hz power in the 8-13 Hz band). And it is built correctly: its DPSS tapers reproduce scipy.signal.windows.dpss to machine precision (~6e-14, the hard eigenvalue computation), its full PSD reproduces an independent scipy+numpy reconstruction of the same algorithm to ~1e-10 (relative ~1e-13), and it agrees with the field-standard MNE psd_array_multitaper in structure (correlation 0.99, up to MNE's one-sided factor-of-2).

claims.statement: dominant frequency of the multitaper spectrum -- the alpha rhythm (Hz)

validation.reference: Two canonical building blocks. (1) scipy.signal.windows.dpss (Virtanen et al. 2020) is the reference DPSS/Slepian taper set; eegMultitaper's tapers reproduce it to max |diff| ~ 6e-14 (the non-trivial tridiagonal eigenvalue computation), and the full non-adaptive PSD reproduces an independent scipy+numpy reconstruction of the identical algorithm to ~1e-10 (relative ~1e-13) -- both machine precision. (2) mne.time_frequency.psd_array_multitaper (Gramfort et al. 2013) is the field-standard multitaper PSD; eegMultitaper agrees with it in structure (correlation 0.99) up to a one-sided factor-of-2 (MNE doubles the positive-frequency power) and a small bandwidth-to-NW convention difference. The finding: an alpha-dominated occipital spectrum (peak 10.5 Hz).
validation.data: REAL -- eegmmidb (PhysioNet), S001 eyes-closed baseline R02, occipital O1, 10 s at 160 Hz
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) eegMultitaper reproduces scipy.signal.windows.dpss (~6e-14) and an independent scipy+numpy multitaper reconstruction (~1e-10) to machine precision, and MNE psd_array_multitaper in structure (correlation 0.99); (2) the eyes-closed occipital spectrum is alpha-dominated (peak 10.5 Hz, 46% of 0-45 Hz power in the alpha band). HONEST scope: (1) TWO machine-precision legs anchor the op -- the DPSS tapers vs scipy (~6e-14) and the full PSD vs an independent from-scratch scipy+numpy reconstruction of the same non-adaptive algorithm (~1e-10, relative ~1e-13); (2) the agreement with MNE psd_array_multitaper is STRUCTURE (correlation 0.99), NOT machine precision -- MNE returns a ONE-SIDED PSD (a factor-of-2: positive frequencies multiplied by 2, so MNE ~ 2x the op) and maps its Hz bandwidth to a slightly different integer NW, so the two differ by a normalization convention + a small taper difference; this is an AGREEMENT leg (like the wavelet-vs-MNE case), reported with the scale factor (~2.00); (3) the alpha-dominated spectrum is the established eyes-closed occipital alpha rhythm -- a validated-estimator demonstration, not a discovery; (4) non-adaptive multitaper, bandwidth NW=4 (7 tapers); (5) single subject/channel, 10 s; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: eegMultitaper is the NON-ADAPTIVE multitaper (equal-weight taper average). The adaptive form (Thomson's iterative eigenvalue weighting, MNE's adaptive=TRUE) down-weights tapers with more broadband leakage and would tighten the estimate near sharp peaks; and a multitaper CROSS-spectrum gives a low-variance coherence (multitaperCoherence, also implemented). Extending this to the adaptive PSD -- pinning the one-sided normalization to MNE's exactly -- and to multitaper coherence would turn a validated estimator into a connectivity tool. Documented, not escalated.
